# Lorenz-63 VPT findings — Track B chaotic metric (Valid Prediction Time)

*Generated by `v3_research/lorenz_vpt.py`. The Track-B brief lists **VPT** as the chaotic-
forecasting metric: the autonomous-rollout horizon at which forecast error first exceeds a
threshold, normalized by the Lyapunov time. Canonical testbed: Lorenz-63 (Ahmed-Tennie-Magri 2025;
Vlachas et al. 2020).*

Setup: Lorenz-63 (σ=10, ρ=28, β=8/3), RK4 dt=0.01, normalized per-dim to [0,1]; λ_max≈0.906 →
~110 steps/Lyapunov time. VPT = first step where normalized error ||pred−true||/RMS > 0.4, in
Lyapunov times, averaged over **25 test initial conditions**, 3 seeds. Autonomous closed-loop
(each model feeds its own prediction back).

## Results

**Static delay-window reservoirs (matched paradigm: window of last 4 states → features → ridge):**

| model | VPT (Lyapunov times) |
|---|---|
| Persistence | 0.07 |
| Linear | 0.20 ± 0.10 |
| **RFF** | **1.18 ± 0.38** |
| CHIMERA | 0.49 ± 0.34 |

**Recurrent reference (different paradigm — internal memory):**

| model | VPT |
|---|---|
| ESN (recurrent, generative) | **2.42 ± 0.58** |

## Verdict (honest, fairly framed)

- **Fair, matched-paradigm test (quantum vs classical, both static delay-window maps):** CHIMERA
  VPT (0.49) does **not** beat the matched classical RFF (1.18) — **no quantum advantage on the
  chaotic VPT metric either**, consistent with every other setting and with the capacity finding.
- **Recurrence dominates chaotic VPT.** The recurrent ESN (2.42) far exceeds *all* static maps —
  for autonomous chaotic rollout, internal recurrence (generalized synchronization, the
  Ahmed-Tennie-Magri mechanism), not the feature map, is what matters. The 0.49-vs-2.42 gap to the
  ESN is therefore an **architecture** difference (static vs recurrent), **not** a quantum-vs-
  classical statement — which is why we report the matched-static RFF as the fair classical bar.
- **Honest open next step:** a *recurrent* (measurement-feedback) CHIMERA is the architecture
  needed to contest the ESN fairly on VPT; the static delay-window quantum map tested here is not
  competitive. Whether a recurrent quantum reservoir closes the gap is genuinely open (and is the
  most likely place, per the literature, for a quantum reservoir to at least be *competitive*).

This adds the Track-B-required VPT metric and keeps the domain-general honest negative intact.
